__TOC__

== Overview ==
This page lists every sound effect a musician can play with [play. Sound effects are written as a plus sign followed by the sound's number, for example:

 [play c 0.3 +480 0.5 e
 +480 plays the client's ''cure'' sound between two notes.

=== Requirements ===
* The 28 percussion sounds (marked ★ below) are free for everyone. Every other sound needs at least 1,000 Music Karma, both to play it with [play and to transcribe it into sheet music (see [[Music Composition#Music Karma|Music Karma]]). Type [play musickarma to see yours.
* Anyone can listen to sheet music that uses sound effects, whatever their karma.
* Sound numbers are decimal and run from 0 to 1487. Numbers outside that range are not played.
* Sound effects follow the same timing, volume (vN) and ConcertMode rules as notes. See [[Music Composition]].

=== Reading the Table ===
* '''Sound''' is the number to use after the + sign.
* '''Hex''' is the same number in hexadecimal, as it often appears in other Ultima Online references.
* '''Name''' is the sound's file name in the game client, which usually describes it (for example ''cure'', ''zombie1'', ''harp01'').
* '''Length''' is the sound's playing time in seconds. Long sounds keep playing under the notes that follow them. The client skips a sound played again too soon after itself (see [[Music Composition#Repeating Notes|Repeating Notes]]).
* Sound 856 has no recording of its own; the client plays sound 550 in its place.
* The instrument notes themselves are in this list too (the ''harp'', ''lap_harp'' and ''lute'' names), but [play's note names are the easier way to play them.

== Percussion ==
These sounds are free for everyone, with no Music Karma needed. They are the clicks, knocks, thuds, swishes, the anvil and the wind chimes, chosen by ear as drums; [[MidiToAIMS]] uses them for a MIDI's drum track.
